extraction_method_note: Per the implementation plan's fallback instruction ('If automatic extraction from specification prose is unreliable, use a reviewed/pinned normalized clause representation instead. Do not hide parser uncertainty.'): every clause below was manually authored by reading erc-4626.raw.md section by section (Methods: asset, totalAssets, convertToShares, convertToAssets, maxDeposit, previewDeposit, deposit, maxMint, previewMint, mint, maxWithdraw, previewWithdraw, withdraw, maxRedeem, previewRedeem, redeem; Events: Deposit, Withdraw; plus the top-level EIP-20-conformance MUSTs and the Security Considerations rounding-direction MUST), not produced by rtf/standards/clause_parser.py's generic RFC2119 extractor. That extractor is built and unit-tested separately (rtf/standards/test_clause_parser.py) against synthetic fixtures to prove the extraction MECHANISM works generically -- it is deliberately NOT run against this real, irregular spec prose for production use, exactly as the plan anticipated real EIP prose would be too irregular for a fully automatic pass (e.g. many clauses share one bare 'MUST NOT revert.' sentence across different methods with no method name repeated in the sentence itself; the round-down guidance in Security Considerations uses lowercase 'should round down' in prose, which the generic extractor correctly treats as non-normative per RFC2119's own capitalization convention -- the actual MUST-round-down obligation is separately and correctly captured per-method under Methods:convertToShares/convertToAssets and again as the explicit cross-function invariant clause 'erc4626-convertto-functions-must-both-round-down' below, both hand-derived directly from the capitalized normative text).
excluded_as_non_normative_note: Explicitly NOT turned into clauses: (1) 'Rationale' section prose (explanatory, no RFC2119 keywords). (2) The lowercase 'it should round down'/'it should round up' generalizations in Security Considerations -- informative discussion in prose, not capitalized SHOULD; superseded by the actual capitalized MUST-round-down clauses on convertToShares/convertToAssets. (3) 'It is recommended that...'/'should be aware' phrasing in Security Considerations -- advisory prose, not a capitalized keyword. (4) 'MUST_NOT' vs 'MUST NOT' is a normalized enum value here, not a textual variant -- the source always writes 'MUST NOT' or 'MUST _NOT_' (italicized in markdown); both are normalized to the same MUST_NOT strength.

clauses.normalized_obligation: Both convertToShares() and convertToAssets() MUST always round down (this restates/reinforces the per-function 'MUST round down towards 0' clauses already captured on each function individually -- kept as a separate clause because the Security Considerations section states it as an explicit cross-function invariant, not merely per-function).

provenance.quoted_text: The only functions where the preferred rounding direction would be ambiguous are the `convertTo` functions. To ensure consistency across all EIP-4626 Vault implementations it is specified that these functions MUST both always round _down_.
